Thursday, November 5, 2026

5:30 pm Conversations | Artist Talk: Linda Bryan Main Gallery- AVA Gallery and Art Center, Lebanon

Free

Artist Talk | Thursday, November 5, 5:30-6:30 pm

In Falling Leaves, Linda Bryan explores the shifting relationship between memory, family, and the objects we use to preserve the past. The exhibition began with the discovery of a handwritten childhood note to Bryan’s mother, prompting questions about memories of family life that no longer aligned with the stories she thought she knew. In this artist talk, Bryan will discuss her process of revisiting family photographs, documents, objects, and ephemera preserved across generations. These materials—some faded, damaged, incomplete, or missing context—become both evidence and reminders of how memory can distort, fragment, and disappear. Bryan will consider how photographs can preserve moments we no longer remember, and how differing recollections among family members can challenge our understanding of the past. Through combining vintage family photographs with images she has made herself, Bryan creates an intimate and evolving visual archive. Falling Leaves considers family history not as a fixed record, but as something continually reconstructed from fragments. The talk offers insight into Bryan’s artistic process and her ongoing exploration of identity, loss, connection, and the uncertain territory between what we remember and what we can prove.

Nov 7 – Nov 8, 2026 Prontoplate at TRPS | 10 AM-4 PM Two Rivers Printmaking Studio - WRJ, VT, White River Jct

Sessions start 10:00 am · $0–$500

Instructor: Liz Bannish

2 Sessions | Nov 7 - 8 | 10 AM - 4 PM

This workshop takes place at Two Rivers Printmaking Studio: 85 N Main St, suite 160, White River Jct, VT, 05001

Lithography was accidentally invented by German playwright Alois Senefedler in 1798 as he was searching for a way to reproduce copies of his scripts. This Prontoplates class will explore polyester plate litho, which can be considered lithography’s modern cousin. This workshop will cover the soup-to-nuts of plate creation and processing, inking and printing, and more. Participants will utilize inexpensive materials such as ballpoint pens, sharpie markers, or laser jet printing to create their plates. The plates can be cut into shapes, support photo-based imagery and can be altered between printings. Discover ink fundamentals, registration tips, and how to print lithographic plates using an etching press. Artists will create unique or editionable prints that can easily incorporate hand drawn or photographic elements, or both. Learn the quick way to litho!

Liz Bannish: https://lizbart.com/

The cost of this workshop is $400; click "Get Tickets" to see that price and other tiered pricing options.

Sunday, November 8, 2026

4 pm - 6 pm The Return (DFS: Myths Revisited) Loew Auditorium, Black Family Visual Arts Center

Ralph Fiennes plays Odysseus in Uberto Pasolini's grounded, realistic adaptation of Homer's dramatic final act.

Stripped of the familiar mythological monsters and gods, Odysseus (Ralph Fiennes) and Penelope (Juliette Binoche) reunite on an Ithaca devoid of the usual fantasy or epic. 
Sweeping visuals are traded for intimate closeups, and the raw, human emotion of Odysseus' return takes center stage rather than its marvel or grandeur. 

Using minimalism, natural light and the story's inherent moral and psychological conflicts, Pasolini crafts a powerful and unforgettable entry into The Odyssey catalog. Fiennes and Binoche carry the film with quiet intensity, making us feel as though we're actually watching the real Odysseus and Penelope reunite. For scholars and cinephiles alike, this is not an adaptation to be missed.

Part of the Dartmouth Film Society series "Myths Revisited"

7:00 pm - 8:30 pm Mary Oliver: Saved By the Beauty of the World Loew Auditorium, Black Family Visual Arts Center

A celebration of Pulitzer Prize-winning poet Mary Oliver, featuring interviews with Oprah Winfrey, Stephen Colbert and dozens more inspired by her work.

Featuring archival footage, never-before-seen personal photos, notebook pages and original interviews, this illuminating documentary explores Oliver's early days as a writer, aspects of her personal life she kept private, and the award-winning works that launched her to broad acclaim. New interviews from Maria Shriver, John Waters, and former US Poet Laureate Ada Limón, as well as poetry recitations from Helena Bonham Carter, Stephen Colbert, Lucy Dacus, Steve Buscemi and Oprah Winfrey reveal the impact of this beloved poet.

"In an era when arts and humanities are on the back foot, Mary Oliver: Saved by the Beauty of the World shows the power of literature and nature to save our souls, one grasshopper, one great love, one poem at a time." Thelma Adams

Nov 13 Nov 18
5:30 pm I Dream Therefore I Am: Women Artists in Surrealism Main Gallery- AVA Gallery and Art Center, Lebanon

Free

Kate Conley, Guest Speaker

I Dream Therefore I Am | Women Artists in Surrealism

Friday, November 13, 5:30-6:30 PM

Surrealism began with friends sitting in the Paris apartment of André Breton in 1922 and experimenting with putting themselves into self-induced trances in an attempt to access their inner beings through a kind of Freudian automatism. Two years later, Breton published the “Manifesto of Surrealism” in which the surrealists jointly declared their wish to integrate dreamlife and the unconscious into our understanding of what it means to be human, to adapt the humanist Cartesian formula “I think therefore I am” into a new version: “I dream therefore I am.” Only men signed the “Manifesto,” but there were always women in the room; women were always part of the surrealist conversation. In a movement founded in friendship, women found their place and by the 1930s, women artists and writers were exhibiting and publishing with their male partners and friends. This talks looks at a series of women artists linked to the surrealist movement from the 1930s to the present day, all of whom sought to define what surrealism was for themselves and, in many cases, what surrealist women looked like and sounded like by providing personalized answers to the dreamy portrayals of women found in the poetry and paintings by men. Leonora Carrington, Dorothea Tanning, Léonor Fini, Remedios Varo, Claude Cahun, Jacqueline Lamba, Lee Miller, Kay Sage, Joyce Mansour, Suzanne Césaire, Frida Kahlo, and Meret Oppenheim all defined what it meant to be a woman in surrealism through their work. As they become increasingly recognized today, more contemporary artists are continuing to advance the legacy of surrealism, including Penny Slinger, Sam Ainsley, Lilia Ziamou, Susanna Wald, and Breton’s daughter Aube Elléouët.

Biography | Kate Conley is Chancellor Professor, Emerita, of French and Francophone Studies at William & Mary and Edward Tuck Professor, Emerita, of French and Comparative Literature at Dartmouth. She is the author of Surrealist Ghostliness (Nebraska, 2013), Robert Desnos, Surrealism, and the Marvelous in Everyday Life (Nebraska, 2003), and Automatic Woman: The Representation of Woman in Surrealism (Nebraska, 1996) and editor and co-editor of books and special issues of journals on women in surrealism, Robert Desnos, and surrealist collecting. She published “From the Studio to the Field: Breton’s ‘Hopi Notebook’” along with her translation of André Breton’s “Hopi Notebook” in the Journal of Surrealism and the Americas in 2023. Her current book project is on “Mapping the Surrealist Collection.” She is co-editor of the International Journal of Surrealism (University of Minnesota Press, 2023-).

7 pm - 9 pm Digger Loew Auditorium, Black Family Visual Arts Center

Tom Cruise plays against type as an aging oil tycoon who must save humanity from his own environmental disaster in Alejandro G. Iñárritu's satirical black comedy.

From Tropic Thunder to Rock of Ages, Tom Cruise has demonstrated that he has range that extends far beyond his action hero persona. Here he takes on the role of aging oil tycoon Digger Rockwell, whose endless quest for wealth and supreme hubris are directly responsible for an impending ecological disaster. Fueled by his narcissism more than altruism, the eccentric billionaire launches a fanatic public crusade to fix the crisis himself.

Director Alejandro G. Iñárritu (Birdman) crafts a cutting satire of catastrophic proportions around Cruise's larger-than-life performance and a stellar supporting cast, including John Goodman, Sandra Hüller, Riz Ahmed, Michael Stuhlbarg, Jesse Plemons and Emma D'Arcy.

Sunday, November 15, 2026

1 pm - 4 pm Met Opera in HD: Carmen (Georges Bizet - Special Encore) Spaulding Auditorium, Hopkins Center for the Arts

A special encore of Richard Eyre's 2010 production of Bizet's masterpiece starring soprano Elīna Garanča as opera's timeless man-eater.

Bizet's masterpiece of the gypsy seductress who lives by her own rules has had an impact far beyond the opera house. The opera's melodic sweep is as irresistible as the title character herself, a force of nature who has become a defining female cultural figure. Carmen was a scandal at its premiere but soon after became a triumphal success and has remained one of the most frequently staged operas in the world.

Elīna Garanča owns the stage as opera's timeless man-eater, with impassioned tenor Roberto Alagna as her lover Don José. Yannick Nézet-Séguin conducts Sir Richard Eyre's powerful production, a Met favorite since its premiere more than 15 years ago.

Tuesday, November 17, 2026

12 pm - 1 pm DCC Grand Rounds with Nancy Lee, MD, FASTRO DHMC Auditorium E

Dr. Nancy Lee is a radiation oncologist who specializes in using advanced forms of radiation to treat Head and neck cancer, including thyroid cancer. She was born in Taiwan and received her bachelor’s degree in chemistry from Barnard College. She earned her MD from the University of Medicine and Dentistry in New Jersey and completed her residency in Radiation Oncology at the Columbia Presbyterian Medical Center. Dr. Lee served as the principal investigator for the Radiation Therapy Oncology Group in a national trial to refine the use of IMRT for treating nasopharyngeal cancer. She is also a member of the RTOG’s Head and Neck Cancer Working Group.

Dr. Lee was a co-author of the Cancer Immunotherapy Guidelines for Head and Neck Cancer put forward by the Society for Immunotherapy of Cancer. She sits on the editorial board of the Journal of Radiation Oncology. She is also the series editor of the Practical Guides in Radiation Oncology.

Saturday, November 21, 2026

2:00 pm - 4:15 pm Broadway in HD: Giant Spaulding Auditorium, Hopkins Center for the Arts

Tony Award-winner John Lithgow embodies children's author Roald Dahl weathering a self-made PR crisis in Mark Rosenblatt's acclaimed play.

It's the summer of 1983, The Witches is about to hit the shelves and Roald Dahl (John Lithgow) is making last-minute edits. But the outcry at his recent, explicitly antisemitic article won't die down. Across a single afternoon at his family home and facing a series of accusations from his inner circle—including his agent and publisher—Dahl is forced to choose: make a public apology or risk his name and reputation. 

"You wait forever for a role like this, full of sadism and monstrosity and hideousness," said John Lithgow, who earned his third Tony Award with this role. It's a performance not to be missed.

Nov 21 – Nov 22, 2026 Etching with BIG Ground & Acrylic Spray Aquatint at TRPS | 10 AM - 4PM Two Rivers Printmaking Studio - WRJ, VT, White River Jct

Sessions start 10:00 am · $0–$438

Instructor: Briony Morrow-Cribbs

This workshop takes place at Two Rivers Printmaking Studio: 85 N Main St, suite 160, White River Jct, VT, 05001

This two-day workshop explores two essential intaglio techniques — hardground line etching and aquatint — using safer, greener materials. We'll begin by preparing copper plates and coating them with Baldwin's BIG ground, a non-toxic alternative to traditional hardgrounds that produces the same wonderfully crisp etched line. Students will draw into the ground, etch their plates, and pull a first proof on the press.

On day two, we'll return to our plates and apply an acrylic aquatint spray to build tone, texture, and depth. We'll be using acrylic spray in place of traditional rosin aquatint — a safer, healthier approach that also opens up exciting possibilities for creating gradients. Through step etching, students will learn to develop a rich range of values on a single plate, from delicate grays to velvety darks.

By the end of the weekend, participants will leave with at least one proof of their plate and a solid foundation in these versatile processes. This workshop is suitable for beginners, though a foundation in etching will be helpful.

2 Sessions | Nov 21 - 22 | 10 AM - 4 PM

Briony Morrow-Cribbs: https://www.brionymorrow-cribbs.com/

The cost of this workshop is $350; click "Get Tickets" to see that price and other tiered pricing options.
